title: Object stuck in a wound (glass, metal, splinter)
summary: Something is embedded in the skin or deeper tissue. Removing it can cause much worse bleeding. Stabilise it and seek medical care.
steps: Do not pull or wiggle the object — it may be pressing on a blood vessel and stopping bleeding.
Sit or lie the person down. Keep them still.
Press firmly around the object — not on top of it — using a clean cloth folded around the object on both sides.
If possible, build up padding around the object so the cloth or bandage does not press the object deeper.
Cover the area loosely with a clean dressing without disturbing the object.
Keep the limb still. Support it with a sling, pillow, or rolled cloth.
Arrange urgent transport to a clinic or hospital.
avoid: Do not pull out the embedded object, even if it looks small.
Do not press directly on top of the object.
Do not give food or drink in case surgery or stitches are needed.
Do not apply ointments, pastes, or home remedies to the wound.
whenToEscalate: Always — embedded objects need professional cleaning and removal under sterile conditions.
Immediately if there is heavy bleeding, the object is in the eye, neck, chest, or abdomen, or if the person feels faint or cold and clammy.
A tetanus check is needed if vaccination is not up to date.
